articles.title: Thousands rally for anti-austerity protest in Brussels amid clashes
articles.summary: Belgian police respond to ‘troublemakers’ on sidelines of main rally with tear gas, water cannon and baton charges.
articles.body:
Clashes have erupted near Brussels Central station on the sidelines of a demonstration organised by the country’s socialist trade union against the federal government’s austerity plans.

As thousands of protesters gathered at the station on Friday, a smaller group clashed with the police and threw wooden beams, glass bottles and rubbish bins, The Belgian Times reported.

Police were deployed in large numbers around the stations as officers checked groups of young people not wearing trade union colours.

Police said the main trade union rally went ahead peacefully but “groups of troublemakers were responsible for serious incidents before and after the march.”

Riot police responded to those protesters with tear gas, water cannon and baton charges. Police said those who “cause the problems of public order are not linked” to the rally.

Reporting from Brussels, Al Jazeera’s Rosie Birchard said damage was caused during Friday morning’s protests with an “acrid smell of burning in the air”, due to fires that were set and the tear gas.

“Police [and] emergency services have been arriving, starting to disperse or clean up and then the protests flare up again. So the day is still early; often these things get worse in the evening in terms of the street violence,” Birchard explained.

“There were some young people who came out, they say they were inspired by what they had seen in France in terms of school protests, and they also wanted to talk about the education environment they’re learning in,” she said, adding that the students felt that they were “not being listened to”.

The clashes came after a week of tension in the city of Liege after authorities banned gatherings as students clashed with police and vandalised shops. More than 200 people were arrested in Liege, and dozens of police were injured.

The ABVV trade union and the Christian ACV, the country’s two biggest unions, organised protests on Friday morning, with protesters marching from Brussels Central station to Brussels South Station under the slogan “stay out of our pockets”.

Police said about 30,000 people attended the demonstrations, while ABVV had earlier estimated attendance at 50,000.

The anger stems from the government’s austerity measures, as officials consider a new budget that opposes potential measures that affect purchasing power, the wage indexation system and value-added tax (VAT), as well as plans to introduce annualised working time.

At the same time, the ACV organised a separate protest involving hundreds of activists at the capital’s headquarters of the governing coalition parties.

articles.title: 'Now feels right to show Bank's Brewery's vital Wolverhampton history'
articles.summary: Tegen Kimbley captured the inner working of the former brewery when she worked at the site in 2018.
articles.body:
A photographer has paid homage to a city's brewing history with an exhibition of behind the scenes images.

Tegen Kimbley was in awe of the Bank's Brewery "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory-esque" design when she started worked at the Wolverhampton site in 2018.

The 30-year-old began taking photos to show the inner workings of the historic landmarks. The display can be viewed at the Wolverhampton Arts Centre until Tuesday. "It feels like the right time to showcase such an important part of Wolverhampton's history," she told the BBC.

Production of Banks's moved to Burton-on-Trent last year, after 150 years in the city.

In other brewing news, Marston's Brewery's owner Carlsberg Britvic announced on Thursday that it was proposing to shut its Burton-upon-Trent facility . About 310 people are affected.

"Another heartbreak in regards to a dying beer trade and ale brewing," said Kimbley.

Kimbley took on a customer service role in her home city after graduating from the University of South Wales.

Seeing the brewery in action rekindled her love for photography and she began capturing the scene in her spare time.

"At the time we had no idea that the brewery was under threat of closing down. I recently went back to take some more photos and it's amazing how much it has changed," she said.

"It's such a shame because it's such an iconic landmark in Wolverhampton and it's the legacy of the area."

The photographer added: "Whenever you speak to anyone about the brewery, they often reminisce about the smell of the hops and being brought up on Banks's Mild. It was a shame to see that part of the city's history disappear.

"It was an important part of Wolverhampton's industrial landscape and its identity. It was part of your every day, it wasn't just a job, it was after work as well when you're in the pub all together enjoying a pint of Banks's."

She added: "I'm extremely grateful I was able to document the inside of this brewery that many people didn't get to see. I was really fascinated by the building, it had a Charlie and the Chocolate Factory-esque about it."

articles.title: Man named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
articles.summary: The left-wing candidate won a narrow victory in a remote district in the Peruvian Andes, exit polls show.
articles.body:
A man named Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores has secured a narrow victory in Peru's local elections, exit polls show.

The candidate for the centre-left Ahora Nación party was elected mayor of Queropalca, a remote district in the Peruvian Andes.

Some 229 residents voted for the 45-year-old, putting him ahead of the second-place candidate from right-wing Renovación Popular Perú by just 25 votes.

Despite being elected to represent fewer than 1,000 people, his forenames being those of two notorious fascist dictators has drawn outsized international attention to the small corner of the country.

Data from Peru's elections office showed a little over 700 people had participated in the election, with Simeon securing around 34% of the vote.

He was born in the district in the central department of Huánuco, some 360km (224 miles) from the capital, Lima, according to his candidate profile.

That he shares his name with Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini - "two of the most well-known figures of 20th-Century European totalitarian regimes" - has made his candidacy a "striking event", local outlet Peru21 reported.

Despite the curiosity generated by his name, local media noted that Hitler Guesclin Alba Sánchez had been elected mayor of Yúngar in 2018.

He reportedly beat rival candidate Lenin Vladimir Rodríguez Valverde after campaigning on the slogan "I'm the good Hitler".

A politician named Adolf Hitler Uunona attracted similar attention in 2020 after winning local elections in Namibia - a former German colony where Adolf and other Germanic first names are not uncommon.

articles.title: Chief secy sends legal notice to Mahua over defamation claims, seeks Rs 10 crore in damages
articles.summary: Bengal chief secretary Manoj Agarwal sends legal notice to TMC MP Mahua Moitra over “vote chor” post, seeks deletion, apology and Rs 10 crore damages.
articles.body: Kolkata: Three days after Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra referred to former state chief electoral officer (CEO) Manoj Agarwal as a “vote chor” and held him responsible for disenfranchising lakhs of valid Bengali voters in a social media post, the latter on Friday sent a legal notice demanding deletion of the post and an earlier one too, seeking an unconditional apology within 24 hours.Agarwal, currently Bengal’s chief secretary, also sought Rs 10 crore in damages for alleged defamation, along with Rs 50,000 towards legal and incidental expenses.Shortly after, Moitra made another post, saying: “Dear Manoj, Where will you spend the ₹10 crores in jail?”In the notice, reference was made to another post made by the MP six days back, when she described Agarwal and assembly election observer Subrata Gupta as the principal architects of Bengal’s SIR exercise.The notice claimed that Moitra’s remarks have damaged Agarwal’s integrity, professional competence and reputation. It also demanded a written undertaking from the TMC MP that she will refrain from making similar allegedly defamatory statements in the future.Agarwal has denied the allegations through the legal notice and maintained that he had neither engaged in electoral fraud nor committed any unlawful act. articles.body: Jaipur: Hopper helpers and drivers in Kishanpole zone went on strike Friday, alleging delays in issuing experience certificates needed for the Rajasthan sanitation workers’ recruitment, with the Oct 13 application deadline approaching.Nand Kishore Dandoriya, president of Sanyukt Valmiki Evam Safayi Shramik Sangh, alleged that zone deputy commissioner Niharika Sharma was not cooperating with workers. He said the strike would continue until the certificates were issued.Sharma denied the allegations, saying applications were being verified before certificates were issued. articles.summary: The alleged hijacker of a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Israel planned to crash the plane into Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion airport with the intention of killing as many people as possible, a preliminary investigation has found.
articles.body: The alleged hijacker of a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Israel planned to crash the plane into Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion airport with the intention of killing as many people as possible, a preliminary investigation has found. The pilot aimed to carry out “a premeditated plot with a terrorist objective, aimed at taking control of the aircraft and using it to carry out a suicide attack targeting the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport,” with the aim of causing “the greatest possible number of casualties,” according to a statement a statement from the United Arab Emirates’ attorney general, who is still investigating the incident.
